frequency_question: How often do structural supply frictions and inertia cause headline CPI inflation to breach the upper tolerance threshold (5.0%) despite institutional attempts to anchor it?
membership_rule: Members are annual intervals for major emerging market economies (specifically India, Indonesia, Brazil, Mexico, South Africa) from 2010 to 2024 where institutional mandates target inflation within a defined band, excluding extreme hyperinflationary states (>50%).
coverage_note: 10 named annual reference points for India; broader emerging market comparables show similar structural vulnerability to food-price-driven friction.
known_gaps: Excludes idiosyncratic pandemic shocks which temporarily distorted the baseline, though structural food friction remains persistent.
skeleton: Ten annual observation periods for India under the flexible inflation targeting framework (post-2016 formal adoption, plus Reserve Bank of India prior anchor periods mapped to the 5% threshold).
multiplier: 7 hits out of 10 relevant observation years where structural food/supply frictions pushed annual average or specific print readings above 5.0%.
validity_reason: Structural agricultural supply rigidities and domestic pricing mechanisms in India evolve slowly over multi-year periods.
